Reference

Core parity requirements

These requirements say that the core plugins keep every feature of Ilium. Each row has an id, a MUST statement, the page that explains it and a test. The ids use the prefix COR. They follow the style of requirements.

Related pages: feature traceability, kernel and boot, config and data migration, CLI compatibility, roadmap.

Id Statement Page where explained Testable how
[COR-001] Every feature F-001 to F-116 MUST behave as in the baseline when its owner is enabled. Feature traceability Run the baseline user-doc scenario for each row against the plugin build and compare the observable result.
[COR-002] Every feature MUST have exactly one owner. Feature traceability Script: count rows per id in the table; the count is 116 and each owner cell is non-empty. The duplicates section lists no open claim.
[COR-003] A row of the traceability table with Kind native-kernel MUST name kernel first in its Owner cell, and every config table named in its Config keys column MUST appear in the key-by-key table of the migration page. Feature traceability Script: parse the table; check the Owner prefix of each native-kernel row; check each named table against the key-by-key table.
[COR-010] Kernel parts MUST stay in the kernel and MUST work with --no-plugins: PTY and vt100, tree model, IPC, snapshot writer, config store, keymap, layout, look painter, scene host, plugin host, recovery page, HTTP listener, kernel CLI. Kernel and boot Start with --no-plugins; attach, create a pane, type, split, detach, reattach and open the recovery page.
[COR-011] Every plugin-owned feature MUST keep its settings, keys, CLI output, data files and defaults. Feature traceability For each plugin, diff the Behaviour contract table against the plugin build: settings rows, key actions, config keys, CLI records and data paths. The diff must be empty.
[COR-020] The server MUST restore the snapshot before any plugin is instantiated, activate startup plugins in dependency order and bind the client socket last. Kernel and boot Spy plugin with startup records the tree at activate; it sees the restored tree.
[COR-021] Exactly the core plugins marked startup MUST be active at boot; the others MUST stay inactive until their trigger fires. Kernel and boot Boot with no client; list active plugin sides; compare with the activation table.
[COR-022] Disabling a core plugin MUST have the stated effect, MUST NOT delete its data and MUST leave the recovery page working. Kernel and boot For each of the 30 plugins: disable it, check the table row, check stored data, open recovery.
[COR-023] The scene world MUST NOT import extensions, and capabilities.scene MUST NOT hold extension grants. Kernel and boot Manifest with extensions.contribute under capabilities.scene fails with manifest.grant-side.
[COR-024] Each change in the live reload and restart table MUST apply as stated. Kernel and boot Change one value of each kind with a client attached; check whether the running side sees it without a restart.
[COR-030] A kernel tab MUST have at most one holder of settings.write-kernel:<tab>. Config and data migration Install two T1 fixtures asking for the same tab; the second fails with manifest.settings-owner.
[COR-031] settings.write-kernel:<tab> MUST be T1 only and high risk; settings.read-kernel:<tab> MUST be open to every tier. Config and data migration T2 with the write grant fails with manifest.grant-tier; T3 with the read grant installs.
[COR-032] Plugin state in a snapshot MUST use snapshot-sections with a schema_version; a section over 256 KiB MUST be dropped without losing the previous value; a failed plugin MUST NOT block the snapshot. Config and data migration Write a 300 KiB section; the previous value survives and the snapshot is written.
[COR-033] The plugin build MUST NOT rename or move any key in config.toml or .ilium/config.yaml and MUST keep unknown keys. Config and data migration Run the build on a config with an unknown key, change one setting, diff the files; only that setting differs.
[COR-040] A plugin MUST declare every ilium subcommand it owns; no built-in command without a declared owner MAY remain. CLI compatibility Compare ilium --help with the ownership table; every non-kernel command names a plugin.
[COR-041] Arguments, options, defaults, output records and exit codes of every command MUST equal the baseline CLI reference. CLI compatibility Replay the examples of cli-reference.md and compare the JSONL records and exit codes.
[COR-042] A disabled or failed owner MUST give exit code 1 and a record with cli.owner-disabled or cli.owner-failed that names the plugin. CLI compatibility Disable chatroom; run ilium chat tail; check record, plugin id and exit code 1.
[COR-043] Every manifest and sample on a core-plugin page MUST pass ilium plugin check with the ilium:plugin@0.1.0 rules. Core plugins Extract the Complete manifest block of each of the 30 pages and run the check; zero errors.
[COR-050] Each of the 30 core-plugin pages MUST hold a Complete manifest section whose sides, worlds, grants and contributions match its tables; the core-plugins index MUST state 30. Core plugins Script: parse each manifest; compare sides and grants with the page tables; compare the index count with the page count; every number of pages stated in core-plugins.md equals the count of core-plugin-*.md files; every cli key in a page's Manifest fragment appears with the same value in its Complete manifest.
[COR-060] The roadmap MUST give each wave a gate test. Roadmap Every wave row has a non-empty gate column that names a test.
[COR-061] The roadmap MUST state what stays native in each wave. Roadmap Every wave row has a non-empty native column.
